audit.why: 52.59% over 2105 games with diff EVEN at 6/10 is right. Riven owns levels 2-6 because every Sett tool is a long cooldown she can bait; Sett owns any trade where she stands still and fills Grit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three level-chart rows disagree with the packet chart. Packet is [Skill, Riven, Riven, Riven, Riven, Riven, Skill]; both layers currently hold [Skill, Riven, Riven, Skill, Skill, Riven, Riven] — rows 3 and 4 are understated and row 6 is overstated.
audit.why: The page's own whys already say Riven at 3 and 4 ('You out-trade a pre-item Sett at this window'; 'Blade of the Exile's extended range keeps you in Q-chain distance ... Wind Slash executes after the bait lands') and say Sett at 6 ('Sett's Show Stopper plus Grit spikes in team fights — take side-lane 1v1s carefully'). Kit backs it: Haymaker 18s and Facebreaker 16s at rank 1 are enormous windows for a champion whose own cooldowns are 13/11/10, so 4-6 is hers; at two items his Grit scales off the HP he buys and hers does not.
audit.corrected: Rows 3 and 4 -> Riven, row 6 -> Skill, in both layers, with phases[6].why rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker is taught as a root that grabs you into the wave (wants.foe[1] 'grab into the wave to root you'). Riot's text: it pulls in all enemies on OPPOSITE sides of Sett and stuns them — 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Alone against him you are slowed, never stunned.
audit.why: This inverts the positioning rule. The page tells you to avoid the wave-side; the truth is the opposite — being the only thing on his side of Facebreaker downgrades a 16-second stun into a slow. It is the single most actionable interaction in the lane and the page has it backwards.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[1] restated as needing you plus a second body on opposite sides; content.early's approach instruction rewritten to 'stay clear of minions so Facebreaker only slows instead of stunning'.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early tells the player 'a spent Haymaker is a dead Sett for the next eight seconds'. Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12 seconds — more than double the stated window at rank 1.
audit.why: Understating the punish window by 10 seconds makes the player re-engage far too cautiously and throws away the entire bait-the-W gameplan the page is built on.

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemization line recommends Plated Steelcaps while the page never states that Haymaker's centre deals TRUE damage — the flagged missing interaction 'resistances-invalidated'.
audit.why: Armour is the wrong answer to the one ability the whole page tells you to respect. The player buys resistances and then dies to a smash that ignores them.
audit.corrected: Stated in content.late: Haymaker's core is true damage, so stacking armour buys nothing against it.

audit.why: All four packet suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES: 'The Show Stopper', 'Show Stopper', 'Sett's Show Stopper' and 'Pit Grit' all match the kit file exactly; the matcher tripped on partial-name forms. No renames made.

edits.before: Level 1 is genuinely even — Sett's Pit Grit passive gives him a beefy double-punch that wins if you let him auto freely, so keep trades to a single Q auto weave and back off rather than committing to a full exchange. At Level 2 the matchup shifts in your favour: you now have W stun, which is the key tool for baiting his Haymaker. Step in, take one auto, dash out with E before his Grit fills enough to hurt, and make him whiff the smash into empty air — a spent Haymaker is a dead Sett for the next eight seconds. At Level 3 your full Q-W-Q-E-Q rotation genuinely threatens a kill if Facebreaker is on cooldown; walk at him from a diagonal so his grab has to predict your path, land W first to lock him in place, and chain the Q sweetspots through him.
edits.after: Level 1 is genuinely even — Sett's Pit Grit passive gives him a beefy double-punch that wins if you let him auto freely, so keep trades to a single Q auto weave and back off rather than committing to a full exchange. At Level 2 the matchup shifts in your favour: you now have W stun, which is the key tool for baiting his Haymaker. Step in, take one auto, dash out with E before his Grit fills enough to hurt, and make him whiff the smash into empty air — a spent Haymaker is a dead Sett for 18 seconds at rank 1. At Level 3 your full Q-W-Q-E-Q rotation genuinely threatens a kill if Facebreaker is on cooldown; stay clear of minions so Facebreaker only slows instead of stunning, land W first to lock him in place, and chain the Q sweetspots through him.

edits.before: In the late game both of you are relevant fighters, but Riven's mobility advantage shrinks somewhat as Sett's raw stats and team-fight Show Stopper become devastating in grouped scenarios. Keep converting your lead into towers and objectives rather than looking for 1v1s through a full item Sett who now stacks enough Grit passively to burst you. In a side-lane 1v1 you still win if you short-trade correctly and avoid his Facebreaker range, but a full team-fight where he lands Show Stopper into your backline erases the individual edge you built. Close the game through mid-lane or take inhibitors — do not let Sett become the late-game team-fight anchor he wants to be.
edits.after: In the late game both of you are relevant fighters, but Riven's mobility advantage shrinks as Sett's raw stats and team-fight Show Stopper become devastating in grouped scenarios. Keep converting your lead into towers and objectives rather than duelling a full-item Sett — Haymaker's centre is true damage, so the armour you stacked buys you nothing against the one hit that matters. In a side-lane 1v1 you still win if you short-trade and stay outside his 490-range Facebreaker, but a team-fight where he lands Show Stopper into your backline erases the individual edge you built. Close through mid or take inhibitors — do not let Sett become the late-game anchor he wants to be.

notes: Sett's R carries a derived 'grounding' flag in the kit file, but Riot's own R text says only 'carries an enemy champion through the air and slams them into the ground, dealing damage and slowing all enemies near where they land' — no grounding, no suppression wording. Per the rule about misfiring flags I trusted the description and wrote nothing about Show Stopper denying your E/Q dashes, even though that would be a high-value line if true. Recorded in unverified. Also: spikes[3].when is 'Lvl 1 / Sett W' while its slot is the late-game spike, so the four spikes read out of chronological order on the page — content is accurate, ordering is not; left alone since fixing it means rewriting a correct spike.
